name: Kazakhstan
eligibility: Closed to international intended parents. A law dated 14 July 2026, No. 350-VIII ZRK, amended the Code on Marriage (Matrimony) and the Family so that only citizens of the Republic of Kazakhstan who are married may be customers of a surrogacy service: the amended article 54 carries that condition in those words, and articles 1 and 57 now define the customer as a citizen who is married. The instrument took effect on 26 July 2026. Foreigners, stateless persons, single women and single men, and unmarried couples are therefore outside the rule, whatever a clinic or an agency may still advertise. Whether agreements made or children conceived before that date were given transitional cover is not established in the sources read, so those are the limits any proposal that puts Kazakhstan in front of you now has to answer against.
paymentModel: The amended text speaks of customers of a surrogacy service, which keeps a paid model for the married citizens it allows, and it requires them to bear the material costs of the carrier's medical examinations. No tariff, cap or wider remuneration rule was readable in the sources opened, so this record states the shape of the model and no figure. Any Kazakh price presented to a foreign family is describing a route the law now closes to them.
parentage: Not established from the sources read, and this record does not assert it. The material opened contains the eligibility provisions and an amendment to the Code on People's Health and the Healthcare System that replaces the assisted-reproduction terminology with extracorporeal fertilisation and transfer and inserts an exclusion reading except for surrogacy. The birth-registration consequences of those changes were not readable, and the state register page for the law itself returned not found when opened, so nothing here states who is named on a Kazakh birth certificate after July 2026.

facts.claim: Law No. 350-VIII ZRK of 14 July 2026 amends the Code on Marriage (Matrimony) and the Family, articles 1, 54 and 57, and article 146 of the Code on People's Health and the Healthcare System. Amended article 54 provides that the citizens of the Republic of Kazakhstan who are married can only be customers of service of surrogacy, and article 146 was amended to insert an exception reading except for surrogacy.

source.label: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 350-VIII ZRK of 14 July 2026
source.publisher: CIS legislation database, a reproduction of official texts of Commonwealth of Independent States states
source.supports: The database reproduction carries the instrument number, the date and the restriction sentence quoted here. Kazakhstan's own legal register page for this law returned not found when opened, so the text is verified through a reproduction of the official translation rather than at the register, which is stated rather than hidden.

facts.claim: President Tokayev signed the amendment on 14 July 2026 and it became effective on 26 July 2026. The report quotes the restriction in Russian: customers of a surrogacy service may only be citizens of the Republic of Kazakhstan who are married.

source.label: Кто может быть заказчиком суррогатного материнства: Токаев подписал закон
source.supports: A Kazakh legal-news outlet reporting the signing and the effective date, published the day after the signature. One international practitioner item gives the signing date as 26 July instead, so this record follows the date shown on the instrument itself and the effective date, and treats the difference as a discrepancy in secondary reporting.

facts.claim: A bar on customers who are not married Kazakh citizens means international intended parents can no longer pursue surrogacy programmes in Kazakhstan, as a legal professional body's news item reports it.

source.label: Kazakhstan bans commercial surrogacy for foreigners
source.publisher: Gazette of the Law Society of Ireland
source.supports: Used only for the effect of the amendment on international programmes, which follows directly from the citizenship and marital conditions in the instrument above. Its description of the amended code as dating from 2011 is not relied on.

timeline.claim: Law No. 350-VIII ZRK, amending the family-code provisions on surrogacy, was signed; its amended article 54 limits surrogacy customers to married citizens of Kazakhstan.
The amendment took effect, closing surrogacy programmes in Kazakhstan to foreigners, single people and unmarried couples.

openQuestions: Whether agreements concluded or children conceived before 26 July 2026 were given transitional cover. Nothing in the material read settles how a family already part-way through a Kazakh programme is treated.
Who is named on a Kazakh birth certificate after the amendment, and whether the intended parents can still be recorded. The registration provisions were not readable here.

What the insertion of except for surrogacy into article 146 of the health code removes in practice, and whether a wider prohibition is contemplated; the December 2025 regulatory moves reported before the law were not documented in a source we could open.
